beats.narration_en: This car just drifted into a concrete wall, but only its tire touched it.
On a flat wall, the same hit lands on the body: front corner first, then the rear.
A Jersey barrier is shaped differently. Its lower face leans back like a steep ramp.
The tire meets that slope first and climbs it, squeezing the suspension.
The slope pushes back on the tire, steering the car toward its lane, body untouched.
That is why this simple concrete shape lines highways and work zones all across America.
